title: Satoshi-era wallet served in a $260 billion lawsuit moves 75 BTC it held since 2011
content: The roughly $5 million transfer also spent the tiny payment used to deliver a court notice to the address in May.

title: Bitcoin miners pay Paraguay $350 million a year, but AI is pushing them out
content: Contracts that sell power to a 4% slice of the world’s bitcoin mining at $44 a megawatt-hour expire on Dec. 31, 2027. Paraguay’s state utility calls the date final, and it has just signed a 15-year deal to power a Founders Fund-backed AI campus.

title: Bitcoin plunges to $68,000 as Anthropic IPO frenzy adds to market jitters
content: Analysts see no direct link between Nvidia and bitcoin's decline, pointing instead to investor capital headed into Anthropic as well as a broader risk-off move.

title: U.S. Senate Banking Committee races toward hearing on new SEC nominations
content: The committee that needs to advance President Donald Trump's nominees responded quickly to set his SEC picks for review next week.

title: Bitcoin heads for sixth weekly loss as Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO looms
content: Bitcoin is down 21% this year as investors weigh Anthropic’s anticipated listing, Nvidia’s leadership upheaval and rising Fed rate hike expectations.

title: Microsoft confirms global outage resolved, rules out cyberattack
content: Microsoft attributed the outage to a network capacity upgrade issue, confirming that the disruption was unrelated to cyberattacks or AI agents.

title: MegaETH parent cuts 20% of staff amid restructuring, AI push
content: MegaETH co-founder Shuyao Kong said the restructuring affected employees who helped build the project’s blockchain, wallet and ecosystem.

title: Bitcoin ETFs shed $2.35B in 2 weeks, BlackRock’s losing streak hits 11
content: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $185.4 million in net outflows Friday, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for $143.5 million and Fidelity’s FBTC shedding $41.9 million.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
content: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

title: OpenAI launches AI payments in ChatGPT with Visa, Mastercard and Amex
content: OpenAI’s new payment wallet lets AI agents complete purchases using existing card networks, with plans to eventually allow preauthorized transactions.

title: Could a Former Nvidia Executive Replace Jensen Huang? Arm’s Rene Haas Emerges as Candidate
content: Nvidia's board has reportedly approached Arm's chief executive as it searches for a replacement for Jensen Huang, while some employees are pushing to bring the chipmaker's founder back as CEO.

title: Should Government Officials Be Banned From Prediction Markets? House Oversight Says Maybe
content: A House Oversight staff memorandum, citing suspicious trades by officials, military personnel and clearance holders, recommends Congress weigh new limits on federal personnel betting on platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket.

title: China’s $3.2 Billion AI Pipeline Still Calls for Nvidia Chips Washington Restricts
content: Chinese data center projects are still being designed around restricted Nvidia processors, even as Beijing pushes domestic alternatives.

title: JPMorgan’s Bitcoin and Crypto-Linked Holdings Approach $1 Billion
content: The bank’s Q3 13F shows roughly $981 million across Bitcoin ETFs, Strategy and Coinbase—likely over $1 billion counting Robinhood and miners.

title: Dormant Bitcoin Wallets Wake Up After 16 Years, Moving $6.9 Million
content: Two Bitcoin mining rewards from September 2010 moved minutes apart. The coins are worth nearly 1.15 million times their original market value.

title: FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch
content: Bitcoin Magazine FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch The Brooklyn company's compact home miner, rated at up to 18 TH/s and starting at $1,099.99, goes on sale Friday at four Micro Center stores, including the chain's new Austin location. This post FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

title: Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double
content: Bitcoin Magazine Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double Robinhood customers traded $17 billion of crypto in October, down 48% from a year earlier, while event contracts traded jumped 136% to 5.9 billion. This post Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .
